Barand Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Sziget utca 1, Hungary

Demolished. Báránd's cemetery was established as early as 1886, per that year's cadastral map; the settlement itself was Roman Catholic church property in the Middle Ages, appearing on the papal tithe list between 1332 and 1336. Information on the town's Jewish community is scarce; its population peaked at 72 in 1910 before declining to 52 by 1941, when 3,798 total residents lived in the town. By 1944, an Orthodox community of 36 members remained, without its own rabbi — the Chief Rabbi of Biharnagybajom served as registrar, and the community's only paid employee was its shochet.
